hypothesis.claim: An exact-ownership managed lease transaction can preserve the existing lease and transition contracts while making every acquisition collision and release cleanup non-destructive to foreign namespace entries.
hypothesis.falsification: Retire this exact transaction if any collision changes a foreign path, any substituted path is unlinked, any normal lifecycle or schema predicate drifts, any partial failure becomes falsely free, or independent normalized replay differs.

changedMechanism: Track creation and exact lock ownership across the managed lease lifecycle; never infer unlink authority from a path name or from entering a broad exception handler.
invariants: Only the managed lease acquisition/release transaction changes.
O_EXCL collision never grants unlink authority over the existing path.
Cleanup requires the retained directory and lock descriptors, device, inode, single-link count, and full random-token payload.
A published lease remains protected by the owned lock until the lease is removed during terminal release.
Lease schema, transition schema, owner and descendant checks, signal authority, evidence contents, and public API remain unchanged.
The canonical live source remains untouched until qm8 terminalizes.
Infrastructure evidence has zero archive, inverse, package-score, compression, or objective authority.

controls.definition: Owned-descriptor manager lifecycle with exact acquisition and release cleanup.
Bound c3cedd46 manager collision path; its broad exception cleanup is the static rejected comparator.
Foreign wrapper owns .lock; manager collision must reject and preserve exact foreign bytes and inode.
First manager owns lease and lock; second manager must reject without changing either.
Lease/lock symlink plus inode, hardlink, and token substitutions must reject without unowned unlink.
Independent fresh local namespaces reproduce normalized receipts, transition shapes, and complete manifests.

population.selection: One normal lifecycle, two collision populations, namespace-type rejections, ownership substitutions, partial-failure states, and independent replay.
population.coordinate: Ordered namespace observation, O_EXCL acquisition, payload fsync, lease publication, owner verification, terminal evidence, lease unlink, exact lock unlink, and directory fsync events.

measurements.definition: Acquire, heartbeat, terminal evidence, release, and reacquire preserve the public contract.

Symlink, inode, hardlink, and token controls reject without unowned unlink.
Every ambiguous post-publication failure remains occupied and auditable.
Lease and transition outputs preserve the bound schema and verifier semantics.
Normalized independent receipts and filesystem manifests agree.
